member.name: T:BlocksOs.Api.RollbarExceptionFilter
member.summary: Reports controller faults to Rollbar. Never alters the response.
member.remarks: A filter rather than middleware, because Genesis registers GlobalExceptionHandlerMiddleware from ConfigureMiddleware -- the last middleware in the pipeline, and therefore the innermost. It turns the exception into a response, so nothing outside it ever sees the throw and Rollbar's own middleware would report almost nothing. The MVC filter stage runs inside all of that, where the exception is still an exception and the request-scoped is still resolvable.

member.name: T:BlocksOs.Api.RollbarSetup
member.summary: Wires Rollbar error reporting into the host.
member.remarks:
Reporting is opt-in. With no Rollbar:AccessToken in configuration every member here is a no-op, so developer machines and any environment that has not been seeded stay silent instead of failing at startup. The token is expected to arrive from the Mongo "Secrets" document (SecretKey "blocks-secret-os") like every other deploy-time value; see .
Rollbar sits alongside the Genesis log pipeline (console/Mongo/LMT) rather than replacing it: Genesis owns Serilog and it is the log store of record. Rollbar exists for alerting and grouping, so it only ever receives faults.

member.name: M:BlocksOs.Api.RollbarSetup.AttachDiagnostics(Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.ILogger)
member.summary: Says in the log whether reporting is on, and surfaces Rollbar's own delivery failures.
member.remarks:
Without this, a token with the wrong scope, a suspended token or a blocked egress route all look identical from the outside: no items, no explanation. Rollbar transmits on a background queue and swallows its own failures by design, so its internal event stream is the only place those show up.
Call after the host is built, so this uses the real logger and lands in the Genesis pipeline (console plus Mongo/LMT) rather than bypassing it.

member.name: M:BlocksOs.Api.RollbarSetup.AddLogCapture(Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.IServiceCollection,Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.IConfiguration)
member.summary: Optionally forwards and above from ILogger to Rollbar.
member.remarks:
Off unless Rollbar:CaptureLogs is true. already reports controller faults with a real exception and tenant context, and Genesis's GlobalExceptionHandlerMiddleware logs those same faults -- so enabling both means two Rollbar items per error. Turn this on to reach faults raised outside the MVC pipeline (middleware, hosted services), accepting the duplicates.
Must be called after ApplicationConfigurations.ConfigureApi: Genesis calls ClearProviders() when it installs Serilog, and logging-builder callbacks run in registration order, so a provider added before that call would be dropped.
